items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to the punishment for
certain traffic infractions committed by an operator of a stretch limousine or
other motor carrier designed or modified for purposes of having a seating
capacity of nine or more passengers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6188

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to the punishment for certain traffic infractions committed by
an operator of a stretch limousine or other motor carrier designed or
modified for purposes of having a seating capacity of nine or more
passengers

 
PURPOSE:

To increase penalties for commercial passenger motor carriers which,make
illegal u-turns, run red lights, or speed with a vehicle designed to
seat nine or more passengers including the driver.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the vehicle and traffic law to expand the u-turn ban
created in the 2019 Adopted Budget to cover any commercial passenger
motor carrier with a seating capacity of nine or more passengers, and
increases the penalties for violating this ban to a penalty of no less
than $250 and/or 15 days' imprisonment for the first offense, with
increased penalties for operating the vehicle with passengers and addi-
tional penalties for multiple convictions within the past 10 years.

Section 2 increases the penalties for commercial passenger motor carrier
with a seating capacity of nine or more passengers which are convicted
for illegally running a red light.

Section 3 provides that commercial passenger motor carriers with a seat-
ing capacity of nine or more passengers which are convicted of speeding
are subject to the enhanced penalty scheme that currently applies to
repeat offenders.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Cutchogue tragedy - which resulted largely from a stretch limousine
committing an illegal u-turn - and subsequent special grand jury report
convened by Suffolk County highlighted the difficulty that employers
face in ensuring that large passenger motor vehicle operators comply
with the traffic laws. Grand jury witnesses testified that they provided
training and prohibited their employees from making u-turns, only to
have those proscriptions ignored.

This legislation increases the penalties for three of the most dangerous
of these moving violations - violations for which the State has even
authorized enforcement cameras to prevent - to provide increased finan-
cial or criminal consequences for committing these dangerous actions,
particularly when an operator has passengers in the vehicle while
violating these laws.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None for State.

 
EFFECTIVE PATE:

Generally one year after being signed into law.

B.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to penalties for
U-turn violations committed by operators of stretch limousines
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6188B

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to penalties
for U-turn violations committed by operators of stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE:

To increase penalties for stretch limousines which make illegal u-turns.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the vehicle and traffic law to expand the u-turn ban
created in the 2019 Adopted Budget to cover any stretch limousine with a
seating capacity of nine or more passengers, and increases the penalties
for violating this ban to a penalty of no less than $250 and/or 15 days'
imprisonment for the first offense, no less than $600 and/or 45 days'
imprisonment for a second offense within 18 months, and a $750-$1000
fine and/or 180 days' imprisonment for operators who are carrying at
least one passenger while violating the u-turn ban.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Cutchogue tragedy - which resulted largely from a stretch limousine
committing an illegal u-turn - and subsequent special grand jury report
convened by Suffolk County highlighted the difficulty that employers
face in ensuring that stretch limousine operators comply with the traf-
fic laws. Grand jury witnesses testified that they provided training and
prohibited their employees from making u-turns, only to have those
proscriptions ignored.

This legislation increases the penalties to provide increased financial
or criminal consequences for committing these dangerous actions, partic-
ularly when an operator has passengers in the vehicle while violating
these laws.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: Similar bill S.6188-A passed Senate without objection.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None for State.

 
EFFECTIVE PATE:

Generally one year after being signed into law.
